question.text: An Indian sponsor wants to raise a Cat III fund with (a) mostly US-based HNIs, (b) a few domestic family offices, (c) a long-short India equity strategy, (d) daily NAV. Which structure is OPTIMAL?

answer.text: Pure onshore AIF only; US HNIs subscribe directly via FPI route into the AIF (unified structure)
Pure offshore fund domiciled in Delaware with no India pooling
Master-feeder: onshore AIF master in India + offshore feeder (GIFT-IFSC or Mauritius) for US HNIs + direct domestic subscription channel
Parallel structure with mirror portfolios — not recommended for long-short strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: The master-feeder structure is a source-supported application here: US HNIs subscribe into an offshore feeder (e.g., GIFT-IFSC or Mauritius) which invests into the onshore Indian master AIF, while domestic family offices subscribe directly into the master. Management fee is charged at the master level with a nominal fee at the feeder. The Trap: Option A (unified) is a possible structure but does not separate the offshore investor pool from the onshore master. Option B abandons the Indian master entirely. Option D's parallel structure runs two portfolios in mirror. Note: The workbook (pp. 128-130) describes master-feeder structure and fee flow that this scenario applies; specific tax-rate optimality claims are not made in those pages.
